reason: The cited evidence (E1) supports that magnetic field treatment can simultaneously improve strength and plasticity in QAl9-4 aluminum bronze via dislocation rearrangement and grain refinement. However, it provides no evidence regarding the retention of a magnetostructural transition or magnetocaloric effect, nor any data on MnNiSi-based alloys. The key premise that the treatment preserves the magnetocaloric effect is entirely unsupported, and the transferability to a different alloy system is assumed without evidence.
premises: Pulsed magnetic field treatment enhances dislocation mobility and rearrangement in alloys
Enhanced dislocation mobility leads to grain refinement and a more uniform dislocation distribution
Grain refinement and uniform dislocations simultaneously improve strength and ductility
Microstructural refinement from magnetic treatment does not disrupt the magnetostructural transition or magnetocaloric effect
These mechanisms observed in other alloys (e.g., QAl9-4) will transfer to MnNiSi-based alloys
